subject: mapping using F2 intercross of natural populations

messages.author: 494a62db3a69fee1
messages.subject: mapping using F2 intercross of natural populations
parts:
I'm using F2 intercross families derived from one pair of wild-caught
F0 to make genetic map and QTL mapping. I'm using SNP markers, so each
locus is bi-allelic (A or B).

This differs from inbred line or RIL in that not all loci in F0 are
homozygous. My current solution is to only use the subset of marker
that are homozygous in F0 (i.e. AA in one grandparent, BB in another).
However, I'm obviously throwing away many markers that were actually
informative for genotype-phenotype association or linkage analysis,
for example, if a locus is AA and AB in F0, the F2 intercross behave
like a back cross . Any way to use all the informative markers in
this kind of crossing scheme using Rqtl? Will other linkage mapping
program, such as JoinMap and MapQTL, better deal with natural
population cross?

Thank you.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] mapping using F2 intercross of natural populations
parts:
It depends on the precise nature of the cross. If a single pair of F1 individuals were used to generate many F2, this corresponds to the phase-known 4-way cross that is implemented in R/qtl. If, on the other hand, the F2 consist of many small sibships from different F1 pairs, then R/qtl likely won't be appropriate.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] mapping using F2 intercross of natural populations
parts: On May 24, 2011, at 11:14 AM, Haili Zhang wrote:
> So, if I use multiple F2 intercrosses from different F1 pairs (single F0 pair), I can only use those markers that are AA and BB in F0, right?
I wouldn't want to do that.

> If I use single F2 familty for a phase-known-4-way mapping, how should I code the genotype in the read.cross function? Since I'm using SNP markers, the F1 cross pair is actually (AxB) x (AxB), rather than (AxB) x (CxD). Could you give me an example read.cross script that describe this kind of genotype?

You need to infer phase, and there's a complicated encoding described in the help file for read.cross (in the section "Value" under "geno".

Call the SNP alleles 1 and 2. For a marker that is (1x2)x(1x2), the offspring genotypes are

11 = AC -> 1
22 = BD -> 4
12 = AD or BC -> 10

If you create a CSV file with this encoding, you can read it in using read.cross, and it should be interpreted as a phase-known 4-way cross (cross type "4way").

You can potentially do a combined analysis of multiple F2 families with R/qtl, but it's not documented and beyond what I want to support at this stage. That is, it can be done, but you'll have to figure it out on your own, as my time is limited.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] mapping using F2 intercross of natural populations
parts:
First, if the two progenitors are heterozygous, then the F1 individuals are not genetically identical which leads to population structure among the F2 individuals that needs to be taken into account. If you don't, you run a serious risk of false positive evidence for QTL.

Second, if there are many markers/regions that are not of the AA:BB type, then by throwing out such regions, you are first throwing away much of your ability to map QTL in such regions.

If at *all* loci that affect the phenotype, the two progenitors are fixed (like AA, BB), then it would be okay to treat the whole cross like a simple intercross between two inbred lines, but if the progenitors are heterozygous for some QTL, you need to deal with these complexities.

karl

messages.author: c68e2a9412504c7a
messages.subject: Re: mapping using F2 intercross of natural populations
parts:
Hi Karl,

I have a somewhat related question to this thread. I have ~9000 markers that have the following genotypes in the P0:

63% aa/bb

24% aa/ab

6% --/ab

5% ab/--

I also have the genotype data for 195 F2 and 20 F1. (The F2 were generated from multiple F1 pairings)

I've done read.cross() on all the F2 genotypes, coding it as F2 intercross. 

The F2 genotypes are as follows, and a plot is attached as well:

 AA:33.8%  AB:46%  BB:20.2%  


However, based on the above thread, it seems that coding all of this data as an F2 intercross is not kosher, correct?

Instead it seems that the easiest thing to do is just focus on the single, largest F2 family. If so, would I code this data as a Backcross, F2, or 4 way cross?


Thank you for your help!

Elisa

On Tuesday, May 24, 2011 2:19:29 AM UTC-7, fishlike wrote:
I'm using F2 intercross families derived from one pair of wild-caught

This differs from inbred line or RIL in that not all loci in F0 are
homozygous. My current solution is to only use the subset of marker

However, I'm obviously throwing away many markers that were actually
informative for genotype-phenotype association or linkage analysis,
for example, if a locus is AA and AB in F0, the F2 intercross behave
like a back cross .  Any way to use all the informative markers in
this kind of crossing scheme using Rqtl? Will other linkage mapping
program, such as JoinMap and MapQTL,  better deal with natural
population cross?

Thank you.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] mapping using F2 intercross of natural populations
parts:
You could focus on just the 63% of markers that are homozygous for different alleles in the P0, and then treat it as an F2.

But if you want to make full use of the data, you'd need to treat it as a 4-way cross.

karl

Hi Karl,

Would I combine each family using c.cross()? 

That requires that each cross have the same number of chromosomes, chr names, same marker orders and positions.

Elisa

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] mapping using F2 intercross of natural populations
parts:
Now that I think about it, you can put them all together. It's just in the phase inference and coding of the genotypes that the sibships need to be considered separately.

But in the QTL analysis, pay attention to the fact that a given QTL may segregate in only a portion of the sibships: just as a marker might be homozygous in an F1 individual, so might the QTL.

I would get the estimated map using the combined sibships, jointly. And I would the same set of markers for everyone, just indicating NA in non-informative cases.

karl
